messages:
Anya: Quick thought — our hotstart path is still getting head-of-line blocking when a big shard gets fetched; wondering if we should choose per-shard concurrency quotas or keep a global priority sort. observations:
Sam: Per-shard quotas avoid one heavy shard from saturating io threads, but hurts throughput if many small shards pile up.
Mike: Priority sorting (by score = pending_bytes / time_budget) helped us earlier for small bursts though it can starve low-priority requests.
Cheng: Hybrid idea: namespace-level concurrency quota + per-request dynamic priority. quota prevents OOM/IO saturation, priority keeps latency-sensitive requests first.
Anya: Can you sketch config? also worried about fairness and cache warming corner cases.
Sam: Example:
```
hotstart:
  ns_quota: 8
  per_shard_quota: 2
  priority_decay: 0.6
  score_factors: [slo_ms:0.5, prefix_miss:0.3, request_age:0.2]
```
Mike: Important: tie-breaker should prefer requests with cached prefix hits to reduce wasted warmups. otherwise we startup a shard for single token and evict it.
Cheng: Telemetry to add: per-shard concurrent_fetches, fetch_wait_time_p90, prefix_hit_after_warmup_pct. Those let us detect noisy shards.
Anya: Also think about fallback policy: if the quota blocks a request beyond X ms, we should fallback to smaller model variant or stream partial weights. Thoughts?
Sam: Agree. Could do fallback chain: stream-index-first -> partial-quant -> model-variant-small. config flag per-customer.
warmup-bot: Summary saved: hybrid quota + dynamic priority + fallback chain. runbook: add alarms on fetch_wait_time_p95 > 200ms and evictions_rate > 1%.
Mike: Next step: I'll prototype scheduling hook in loader (tiny PR) that returns a priority score and a boolean allowed_by_quota. will share perf microbench.
Anya: Perfect. if you can include a tiny sim where one large shard and 100 small shards compete, that'll tell us tradeoffs.
Sam: +1
Cheng: I'll draft an RFC blurb with telemetry defs + runbook entries.
Anya: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
